Basal metabolic rate measurements in the Hairy-legged vampire bat (Diphylla ecaudata) were obtained through flow-through respirometry on post-absorptive, resting individuals during their inactive phase. At a controlled ambient temperature of 32.4 °C [T = 32.4 °C], the maximum resting oxygen consumption was recorded as 38.6 milliliters of oxygen per hour [JOi = 38.6 milliliters of oxygen per hour], a value derived from corrected PNAS tables that account for the species' unique sanguivorous physiology. This relatively modest metabolic rate, compared to other chiropterans of similar size, reflects the energetic constraints imposed by a diet consisting exclusively of blood, which is low in carbohydrates and lipids. The measurements were taken during the daytime roosting period when the bats were thermoconforming, a state that reduces thermoregulatory costs and allows for a standardized assessment of basal energy demand. This finding aligns with the general pattern observed among obligate blood-feeders, where metabolic suppression represents an adaptive strategy for managing the irregular availability of vertebrate hosts.

Neonatal development in Diphylla ecaudata begins with a notably small birth mass, as newly emerged pups weigh approximately 4.8 grams [Wwb = approximately 4.8 grams], a value that represents less than fourteen percent of the adult female's body weight. This altricial condition necessitates an extended period of intense maternal care, with the initial phase focused entirely on lactation and thermoregulatory support within the roost. The pups are born with their eyes closed and sparse fur, entirely dependent on the mother for nourishment and warmth during the first weeks of life. Births appear to be synchronized with periods of peak host availability, ensuring that lactating females can meet the elevated energetic demands of milk production. Observations of captive colonies confirm that successful rearing of a single offspring per reproductive event is the norm, with twinning reported only rarely in this species.

Weaning represents a critical developmental transition in the life cycle of the Hairy-legged vampire bat, occurring at 57 days from birth [tx = 57 days from birth] when maintained at a roost temperature of 32.4 °C [T = 32.4 °C]. At this stage, the weanling reaches a wet weight of 21.9 grams [Wwx = 21.9 grams], indicating that the juvenile has attained roughly sixty-three percent of the ultimate adult mass. The process of dietary transition from milk to blood is facilitated by behavioral transmission from the mother, as the pup observes and mimics the specialized tongue movements required to lap blood from a host wound. This social learning period is essential, given the highly specialized foraging technique that characterizes adult hematophagy. Juveniles that fail to acquire this skill within the first few weeks post-weaning exhibit reduced survival rates in the wild, highlighting the importance of maternal tutelage during this vulnerable stage.

Reproductive timing in Diphylla ecaudata exhibits a slow pace typical of long-lived bats, with females producing a single pup per litter [N_R_i = single pup per litter] and at most one litter per year [F_R_i = one litter per year] at the stable temperature of 32.4 °C [T = 32.4 °C] that characterizes their thermally buffered cave roosts. This low intrinsic rate of increase is partly offset by high adult survival, as the species can achieve a maximum lifespan of 8 years [am = 8 years] under natural conditions, a longevity that permits multiple reproductive attempts over a lifetime at a temperature of 32.4 °C [T = 32.4 °C]. The gestation period, estimated from the closely related common vampire bat Desmodus rotundus, spans approximately 168 days [tg = approximately 168 days] at 32.4 °C [T = 32.4 °C], reflecting the challenges of supporting a growing foetus on a low-energy diet. This extended pregnancy imposes significant energetic costs on the female, who must increase her nightly feeding frequency to sustain both herself and the developing offspring.

Sexual maturation in the Hairy-legged vampire bat is a gradual process, with puberty attained at approximately 365 days after birth [tp = approximately 365 days after birth] in the thermal environment of the roost at 32.4 °C [T = 32.4 °C]. This relatively late age at maturity, combined with the single-offspring reproductive strategy, classifies Diphylla ecaudata as a typical K-selected species among bats. The ultimate adult wet weight for healthy individuals reaches approximately 35 grams [Wwi = approximately 35 grams], though field measurements of wild-caught adults range from 24 to 43 grams depending on nutritional condition and reproductive status. The interplay between a low metabolic rate, extended developmental periods, and a specialized trophic niche has shaped a life history that prioritizes individual survival and iteroparity over high fecundity, a strategy well-suited to the stable but resource-limited environment these bats inhabit.
